intro.title: Infrastructure as Code
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll learn Infrastructure as Code (IaC) by creating a simple cloud server configuration using declarative code. You'll understand how IaC allows you to manage infrastructure through machine-readable files instead of manual processes. The core concept is treating infrastructure setup like software development—using version control, testing, and automation. You'll work with basic configuration files that define server properties and dependencies. This approach ensures consistent, repeatable, and scalable infrastructure deployments. By the end, you'll see how IaC reduces human error and speeds up environment provisioning.
intro.usecase: Infrastructure as Code (IaC) is the backbone of modern cloud infrastructure management, appearing in platforms like AWS CloudFormation, Terraform, and Azure Resource Manager. Developers use IaC to define entire server environments, networking configurations, and security policies through code templates instead of manual console clicks. This enables consistent deployment of production environments, automated scaling of web applications, and reproducible disaster recovery setups. In practice, you'll see IaC managing everything from Kubernetes clusters for microservices to complete CI/CD pipeline infrastructure, ensuring that every deployment is identical, version-controlled, and auditable.
